subject.title: [Feature]: Webhook hook sessions should reuse existing session when sessionKey is consistent (multi-turn support)

question: Should authenticated hook-agent requests be allowed to re-enter stored sessions through an explicit persistent mode, and must reuse be limited to hook-owned allowed-prefix keys rather than arbitrary existing channel sessions?
rationale: The implementation gap is clear, but choosing the reusable session namespace determines whether external webhook content can cross conversation, agent, and delivery boundaries.

options.title: Approve hook-scoped persistence
options.body: Add explicit persistent mode with isolated default, retain hook authentication and allowed-prefix checks, and limit reuse to hook-owned session keys.

options.title: Keep hooks isolated
options.body: Continue creating fresh sessions for hook-agent runs and revise documentation to clarify that stable keys do not preserve transcript continuity.

options.title: Allow general session re-entry
options.body: Permit trusted hooks to target existing agent or channel sessions with a broader authorization policy and dedicated cross-channel security tests.

recommendation.title: Approve hook-scoped persistence
recommendation.body: Add explicit persistent mode with isolated default, retain hook authentication and allowed-prefix checks, and limit reuse to hook-owned session keys.

likelyOwner.reason: He already documented the preferred compatibility shape and is the strongest available routing candidate for the remaining product and security boundary.
